newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - JULY 10.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Floods spread yesterday to Olomouc, Hradec Kralove, part of Brno, Kromeriz, Blansko and Adamov. Environment Minister Jiri Skalicky confirmed officially that nine people are dead and four missing, although the fire department and the police say 16 are dead.
- The central bank eased its repo rate yesterday by 0.3 percentage points to 16.2 percent. The crown remained stable.
- The cabinet decided yesterday to provide several hundreds of millions of crowns to help people in flooded areas. Parliament will provide another 900 million crowns.
- The radical wing of the Czech Medical Chamber called for the chairman of the chamber, Bohuslav Svoboda, to resign because he agreed to 77 hellers per point instead of one crown.
- Kaucuk a.s. signed a seven-year syndicated loan of 250 million marks with a consortium of 14 foreign and two domestic banks.
- The German Environment Ministry will provide 4.4 million marks for a pilot project of an environmental heating and power plant in Cheb, western Bohemia.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Hydrometeorologists announced yesterday that floods in the east of the country are higher than any other so far this century.

- From next Monday, Ceska Sporitelna will begin offering credits for repairs and reconstruction of up to 100,000 crowns, valid for eight years with a 10 percent interest rate, for citizens who suffered because of the floods.
- Agriculture Minister Josef Lux estimates that flood damage in agriculture so far is 1.5 billion crowns on the fields and about 100 million for other farming production.
- Yesterday, parliament approved a law to issue government bonds to finance the budget deficit from last year of 11 billion crowns.
- By the end of this month, Foresbank Zlin should obtain a strategic partner, which will buy 44 percent of its shares through Forest Group.
- After two years and eight months, the Slovak National Property Fund transferred 51 percent of Novacke Chemicke Zavody to Prague's Inekon.

- Norwegian Rieber and Son obtained a 100-percent share in the largest domestic spice company, Emarko Varnsdorf, which will be added to a group containing Vitana and Bask, creating the second largest food company in the Czech Republic.
PRAVO - During the first quarter of this month, Daewoo Avia increased output of automobiles by 8.5 percent, year-on-year, and sales by 18.5 percent.
- The chairman of the board at Ceska Pojistovna, former Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik, estimates initial damages from the floods at around 50 billion crowns.
- President Vaclav Havel will visit the areas most affected by the floods today.
LIDOVE NOVINY - For the first quarter of this year, investment funds and companies had profits of 4.2 billion crowns, a year-on-year loss of 6.3 billion crowns.
- From the beginning of the Support and Guarantee Field and Forest Fund in March 1994 until June 8 this year, the fund provided farmers with about 43.1 billion crowns.
- According to a law approved by parliament yesterday, deputy ministers can no longer function as parliamentary representatives or senators.
-- Prague Newsroom, 420-2-2423-0003
